key_insight: Shallow neural networks tend to learn sinusoidal, low-frequency components first because the gradient-descent dynamics in an orthogonal polynomial basis have a graded matrix structure with rapidly decaying eigenvalues.
engineering_relevance: This gives practitioners a more general theoretical lens for predicting and interpreting spectral bias across activations like sigmoid and ReLU, not just in Fourier-domain toy settings.
method: Expand network outputs as a general Fourier series in an orthogonal polynomial basis
Derive ODEs for gradient-descent dynamics of the expansion coefficients
Analyze the dynamics matrix H via eigenvalue decay and eigenvector structure to explain learning order
evidence_signal: The paper is theory-driven and supports its claims by analyzing the structure of H rather than reporting new experimental datasets in the abstract.
watch_item: The framework is asymptotic and analytical, so practical fidelity may depend on how well the polynomial-basis assumptions and weak data-distribution conditions hold in real training settings.
paper_title: Why Shallow Neural Networks Learn Sinusoidal Components First: An Orthogonal Polynomial Dynamics Framework
